title: Philippines to Kuwait domestic-work corridor
summary: Public-source reference for the PHL to KWT domestic-work corridor: legal placement-fee cap, contract-substitution patterns, and verified complaint channels.

source.citation: Composite citation for the public hub demo. Replace with the live regulator URL before partner use.

review_notes: Cross-checked the placement-fee cap against the source-country bilateral agreement.
Removed one citation that pointed to an expired regulator URL.

sections.heading: Legal placement-fee cap
sections.body: Workers travelling on this corridor for domestic work are not legally required to pay a placement fee to a private recruiter beyond the regulated cap. The host-country employer covers the recruitment cost under the bilateral agreement. Any fee request above the cap is treated as a recruitment-fee violation.

sections.heading: Contract-substitution patterns
sections.body: Common substitution patterns: a worker signs a model contract before departure, then is asked to sign a second contract on arrival with reduced wages, longer hours, or a different employer. The second contract is generally not enforceable in either jurisdiction; the model contract remains the reference.

sections.heading: Passport handling
sections.body: Employers may not lawfully retain a worker's passport. Workers should keep their passport in their own possession. If an employer or agency retains it, that is an indicator of forced-labour risk and grounds for a complaint to the regulator.
